sources.note: Nothing; classification (McDowell & Anderbeck 2020; Asmah Haji Omar 1985), AES 'threatened', alternative names (Lembak, Linggau, Sindang, Col/Cul/Kol/Kor). Descriptive bibliography = the three Pusat Bahasa volumes only.

sources.citation: Noermanzah. 2017. Struktur kalimat tunggal bahasa Sindang di Kota Lubuklinggau dan pengaruhnya dalam pembelajaran bahasa Indonesia. AKSIS: Jurnal Pendidikan Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia 1(1): 1-26. doi:10.21009/AKSIS.010101
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; syntax of simple sentences. Only prosodic remark is generic sentence intonation of vocatives ('intonasi naik', 'turun-naik'), copied from Indonesian grammar tradition.

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl (submitter). 2007. ISO 639-3 change request 2007-196: merge [sdi] Sindang Kelingi into [liw], rename Lembak to Col. SIL International / ISO 639-3 RA. Effective 2008-01-14.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress. Gives language identity (Col = Sindang = Lembak; dialects Sindang Kelingi Ilir, Sindang Kelingi, Sindang Beliti, Saling, plus Lembak Delapan near Bengkulu city), survey dates 2005-2007, and a bibliography naming Arifin et al. 1996, Arifin et al. 1997, McDowell (forthcoming) South Sumatran Survey Report, and Aliana et al. 1984 (Belide dialek Lembak, a Musi lect, not Col).
Nothing; only the note that Lembak uses final -e (taling), e.g. apa > ape [ape]. Cites Ethnologue, Joshua Project, Glottolog only.
